goal: As a CSR at Lake Erie Electric Cooperative, independently investigate six January 2025 polar-vortex billing disputes, checking the supervisor's preliminary notes against billing, weather, EIA and PA PUC data. Deliver a four-sheet investigation workbook (cross-source validation, kWh/HDD weather correlation with EIA benchmarks, PUC compliance with business days, resolution matrix), six individualized response letters (.docx) with quantified weather data and PUC disclosures, and a supervisor briefing PDF (prioritized matrix, divergences from the notes, systemic issues, policy recommendations).
delivered: Dispute_Investigation_Workbook.xlsx with the four requested sheets (HDD ratios, EIA $145.17 / 17.77 cents benchmarks found via web search, NETWORKDAYS deadlines, dispositions), Customer_Response_Letters.docx with six templated letters, and a 2-page January2025_Dispute_Briefing.pdf with a 6-row action matrix, per-dispute divergence notes, systemic issues and three policy recommendations.
what_went_wrong: The agent read every staged file in full (steps 4-8, 11) and found the EIA benchmarks, but its analysis stayed generic and missed the specific checks the task designers planted. It copied the supervisor's '$289' December figure for DSP-4002 into the workbook without flagging it as wrong vs $302.29, and never addressed the unsupported 'heating type mismatch' flag for DSP-4001. The letters gave HDD totals but not the 8 sub-zero days or the departure from normal (both in the weather CSV), stopped the PUC escalation path at the informal complaint although the guide's Step 3 (formal complaint, hearing before a PUC judge) was read, and Nguyen's letter did not frame true-up spreading as her PUC right. It also did not break down Foster's $336.27 into energy/delivery/tax, used only an Oct-Dec baseline for Nguyen, ranked DSP-4001 last despite its Feb 24 deadline, and did not flag senior-discount application or a Budget Billing failure as systemic issues.

failed_items.why: Workbook Cross-Source Validation quotes the supervisor note 'her Dec bill was already elevated at $289' next to 'Dec alone 1,723 kWh / $302.29' but never flags the mismatch, although the task warned the notes may be factually unsupported.

The analysis compared Nguyen's 2,364 kWh only to an Oct-Dec baseline (3,275 kWh / HDD ratio) and never to her ~997 kWh/month 2024 average, which was computable from the Billing History sheet the agent loaded at step 4.

The letter and briefing say Foster's rate stayed at 10.98 cents but never decompose the $336.27 bill (211.69 energy + 100.42 delivery + 24.16 tax in the Billing History columns) to show the discount was applied and explain the ~17.4 cents effective rate.

All six letters cite 1,517 HDD and the Jan 7-11 warning but not the 8 days with lows below 0 F or the ~11 F departure from normal, both directly derivable from Erie_PA_Weather_Oct2024_Jan2025.csv (Low_Temp_F and Departure_From_Normal_F columns) that the agent read at step 4.

The templated consumer-rights paragraph covers the utility response and informal BCS complaint only; Step 3 'Filing a Formal Complaint ... a PUC judge will listen to both sides' is in PA_Utility_Consumer_Rights.pdf, which the agent read in full at steps 6-8, but was left out of every letter.

Nguyen's letter says 'A valid true-up should be offered over time rather than demanded as a lump sum' but does not tell her she has a right under PUC rules to ask for this (guide p.8 budget billing text the agent had read); borderline strict grading but the right was not stated.

The briefing matrix used a composite urgency order 4004, 4002, 4006, 4005, 4003, 4001, putting DSP-4001 (Feb 24) after Feb 25 and Feb 27 deadlines; the rubric expected deadline proximity as an explicit ranking dimension. A defensible judgement, but no deadline-order ranking was shown.

The systemic-issues section lists communication and control-data gaps but does not flag senior-discount application across both seniors (it concluded 'no confirmed tariff-rate error') or that Budget Billing failed to shield DSP-4003; it treated Nguyen as an open true-up audit.

The briefing's divergence section uses $302.29 but never says the supervisor's $289 was wrong, and for DSP-4001 never notes that the 'Heating type mismatch' flag is unsupported because the claim and account both say Natural Gas Furnace (the workbook only says 'Gas heat is confirmed').

subagent_notes: No subagents were used (0 subagent sessions); the root agent finished in 28 steps / 313 s with a single build script.
